newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--back to unchanged after data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS--back to unchanged after data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds, after a brief pop higher in early trading, moved back to Monday's levels in choppy action Tuesday.
Traders said municipal prices rose as much as three or four basis points shortly after April retail sales figures were released at 0830 EDT.

The Commerce Department said retail sales fell 0.3 percent last month, exactly in line with expectations. Excluding the automobile component, however, sales fell 0.1 percent, versus forecasts calling for a 0.1 percent rise.
Treasury securities also moved higher after the data, but eventually surrendered the gains. The long bond was down 6/32 at 96-16/32 to yield 6.90 percent.
Municipals have not moved into negative territory yet, and traders said the slim new issue calendar might be helping to lend price support.
"The market doesn't look like it's going to go down, just because of the lack of supply at the moment," one trader said.
Tuesday's new offerings are expected to total $840 million in 40 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Negotiated offerings total $385 million in eight sales. Dillon, Read & Co. tentatively priced the day's largest, a $198 million Ocean County Utility Authority, N.J. deal, at a top yield of 5.45 percent in 2013.
On the competitive side, 32 sales totaling $455 million are scheduled. A $139 million Cleveland City School District, Ohio, deal at 1100 EDT is the largest.
In debt futures, June municipal bonds were down 10/32 at 115-20/32. The June T-bond contract was off 11/32 at 110-1/32. The MOB spread widened to 179 ticks from 178 at the close on Monday.
In muni secondary action, bids on Chicago Board of Education AMBAC 5-3/4s of 2027 were unchanged at 5.86 percent. Port of Seattle FGIC 5-1/2s of 2022 were down two basis points at 5.77 percent.
